title: Swedish society: nature, welfare and the ballot box
goal: Discuss the pillars of Swedish society — the right of public access, the welfare state, elections and the climate debate — with the vocabulary and sentence patterns of an informed adult.
bekal: you can explain what *allemansrätten* allows and forbids
you can talk about rights and duties: *ha rätt att*, *vara skyldig att*, *det är förbjudet att*
you can describe trends and take part in a dinner-table debate about taxes, elections and the climate
wave: Go back to Unit 9: make one sentence about Sweden with each of *på grund av*, *trots*, *med tanke på*, *när det gäller* and *i förhållande till* — for example *Trots de höga skatterna är många nöjda med välfärden.*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — En natt på ön
dialogs.intro: A warm Saturday in August. Dian, Elin and Oskar have paddled kayaks out into the Stockholm archipelago and are looking for a place to spend the night. Dian is not quite sure what they are allowed to do.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Här! Den här lilla ön är perfekt. Vi slår upp tältet bakom tallarna.
lines.id: Here! This little island is perfect. We'll pitch the tent behind the pines.
lines.literal: here! this here little island-the is perfect. we strike up tent-the behind pines-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Får man verkligen tälta var som helst? Ön måste väl tillhöra någon?
lines.id: Are you really allowed to camp anywhere? The island must belong to someone, surely?
lines.literal: may one really camp where as ever? island-the must surely belong-to someone?

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Jo, men tack vare allemansrätten får vi stanna en natt, så länge vi inte stör eller förstör.
lines.id: It does, but thanks to the right of public access we can stay one night, as long as we don't disturb or destroy anything.
lines.literal: yes, but thanks to everyman's-right-the may we stay one night, so long we not disturb or destroy.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: "Inte störa, inte förstöra" — det lär sig varenda unge i skolan.
lines.id: "Don't disturb, don't destroy" — every single kid learns that at school.
lines.literal: not disturb, not destroy — that learns every-single kid in school-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Men det där huset på udden då? Är vi inte för nära?
lines.id: But what about that house on the point? Aren't we too close?
lines.literal: but that there house-the on point-the then? are we not too near?

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Bra fråga. Man ska hålla sig utanför tomten och inte synas från fönstren. Här är vi långt borta.
lines.id: Good question. You have to stay off the private grounds and not be visible from the windows. Here we're far away.
lines.literal: good question. one shall keep oneself outside plot-the and not be-seen from windows-the. here are we far away.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Får vi göra upp eld också?
lines.id: Are we allowed to make a fire, too?
lines.literal: may we make up fire also?

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Bara om det inte är eldningsförbud. Jag kollade länsstyrelsens sida i morse — inget förbud idag.
lines.id: Only if there's no fire ban. I checked the county board's website this morning — no ban today.
lines.literal: only if it not is burning-ban. I checked county-board-the's page this-morning — no ban today.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Och aldrig direkt på berghällen. Den spricker av värmen och blir förstörd för all framtid.
lines.id: And never directly on the bare rock. It cracks from the heat and is ruined forever.
lines.literal: and never directly on rock-slab-the. it cracks of heat-the and becomes destroyed for all future.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det är ganska unikt, faktiskt. I många länder skulle man bli polisanmäld direkt.
lines.id: It's pretty unique, actually. In a lot of countries you'd be reported to the police right away.
lines.literal: it is rather unique, actually. in many countries would one become police-reported directly.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Det bygger på förtroende. Friheten kräver att alla tar ansvar.
lines.id: It's built on trust. The freedom requires everyone to take responsibility.
lines.literal: it builds on trust. freedom-the demands that all take responsibility.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Precis. Och i gengäld tar vi med oss allt skräp när vi åker härifrån — även andras.
lines.id: Exactly. And in return we take all the litter with us when we leave — even other people's.
lines.literal: exactly. and in return take we with us all trash when we go from-here — even others'.

notes: **Allemansrätten** (**AHL-leh-mahns-ret-ten**), "everyman's right", is not a single law but an old custom, written into the Swedish Constitution since 1994. It lets everyone walk, cycle, paddle, swim, pick berries and mushrooms, and pitch a tent for a night or two on land they don't own. The motto *inte störa, inte förstöra* sums up the duties that come with it.

**Var som helst** = anywhere. The pattern *question word + som helst* is extremely productive: *vem som helst* (anyone at all), *vad som helst* (anything), *när som helst* (any time), *hur som helst* (anyway). **Måste väl** — the modal particle *väl* (Unit 5) asks for confirmation: "surely it must…?"

**Tomten** here is not Santa Claus (*tomten*) but *tomt*, the plot or grounds around a house. The area closest to a home, where people can expect privacy, is called *hemfridszonen*, and allemansrätten does not apply there. There is no fixed distance — common sense decides.

**Eldningsförbud** (**ELD-nings-för-büd**), a fire ban, is decided by the **länsstyrelsen** (county administrative board) or the municipality during dry periods, and it applies to everyone — even on your own land. Sweden has 21 *län* (counties), each with its own *länsstyrelse*.
**Det lär sig varenda unge** — the object *det* is fronted (Unit 1), and *varenda* (**vahr-EN-dah**) means "every single", stronger than *varje*. *Unge* is an informal word for a child, like "kid".

**I gengäld** (**ee YEHN-yeld**) = in return. **Polisanmäld** (reported to the police) is the participle of *polisanmäla*; with *bli* it forms a passive of what happens (Svenska 102, Unit 6): *man skulle bli polisanmäld*.

grammars.title: Rights and duties
body: Talking about society means talking about what people may, must and must not do. Swedish has a ladder of expressions, from the everyday to the official.

head: Expression
Meaning
Example
rows: Alla **har rätt att** röra sig i naturen. Alla **har rätt till** vård.
Markägaren **är** inte **skyldig att** städa efter dig.
**Det är förbjudet att** köra bil i terrängen.

after: Remember that *får inte* means "must not", while *behöver inte* means "don't have to" (Svenska 102, Unit 11). *Man får inte elda* = it's forbidden; *man behöver inte elda* = there's no need.
*Skyldig* also means "guilty" and "owing": *Jag är skyldig dig hundra kronor* (I owe you a hundred kronor). The common idea is a debt — of money, of duty, or of guilt.
*Tvungen* agrees with the subject: *jag är tvungen*, *det är tvunget*, *vi är tvungna*.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Middag hos Anna och Lars
dialogs.intro: Sunday dinner at Elin's parents' house in Bromma. Over the main course, Lars turns to Dian with a big question — and the table soon divides along familiar lines.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Nå, Dian, nu när du har bott här i några år — vad tycker du om det svenska samhället?
lines.id: So, Dian, now that you've lived here for a few years — what do you think of Swedish society?
lines.literal: well, Dian, now when you have lived here in some years — what think you about the Swedish society-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Mycket fungerar bra. Föräldraledigheten, den avgiftsfria utbildningen… Men skatterna är ju höga.
lines.id: A lot of things work well. The parental leave, the free education… But the taxes are high, of course.
lines.literal: much works well. parental-leave-the, the fee-free education-the… but taxes-the are you-know high.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Höga, ja. Men vi får något för pengarna. Det är själva grundtanken med välfärdsstaten.
lines.id: High, yes. But we get something for our money. That's the very idea behind the welfare state.
lines.literal: high, yes. but we get something for money-the. that is very basic-idea-the with welfare-state-the.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Det beror på vem man frågar. Vårdköerna har blivit längre, och många upplever att skolan har blivit sämre.
lines.id: That depends on who you ask. Waiting lists for healthcare have got longer, and many people feel the schools have got worse.
lines.literal: it depends on who one asks. care-queues-the have become longer, and many experience that school-the has become worse.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Mamma, du låter som en valaffisch!
lines.id: Mom, you sound like an election poster!
lines.literal: mom, you sound like an election-poster!

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Ha! Men det är just därför valdeltagandet är så högt här. Folk bryr sig.
lines.id: Ha! But that's exactly why the turnout is so high here. People care.
lines.literal: ha! but it is just therefore election-participation-the is so high here. people care themselves.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hur högt är det egentligen?
lines.id: How high is it, actually?
lines.literal: how high is it actually?

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Runt 85 procent i riksdagsvalet. Och vi röstar till riksdag, region och kommun samma dag.
lines.id: Around 85 percent in the general election. And we vote for parliament, region and municipality on the same day.
lines.literal: around 85 percent in parliament-election-the. and we vote to parliament, region and municipality same day.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Imponerande. Och vad röstar unga på? Elin säger att klimatet är den viktigaste frågan.
lines.id: Impressive. And what do young people vote for? Elin says the climate is the most important issue.
lines.literal: impressive. and what vote young on? Elin says that climate-the is the most-important question-the.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: För mig, ja. Vi kan inte fortsätta att flyga och köra bil som om ingenting hade hänt.
lines.id: For me, yes. We can't keep flying and driving as if nothing had happened.
lines.literal: for me, yes. we can not continue to fly and drive car as if nothing had happened.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Samtidigt måste omställningen vara rättvis. Folk på landsbygden är beroende av bilen.
lines.id: At the same time, the transition has to be fair. People in the countryside depend on their cars.
lines.literal: at-the-same-time must transition-the be fair. people on countryside-the are dependent of car-the.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Där har du hela debatten i ett nötskal. Ska vi ta efterrätten innan det blir regeringskris vid bordet?
lines.id: There's the whole debate in a nutshell. Shall we have dessert before we get a government crisis at the table?
lines.literal: there have you whole debate-the in a nutshell. shall we take dessert-the before it becomes government-crisis at table-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Gärna! Men jag vill höra fortsättningen sen.
lines.id: Yes, please! But I want to hear the rest later.
lines.literal: gladly! but I want hear continuation-the later.

notes: **Skatterna är ju höga** — *ju* (Unit 5) marks something both speakers know: "as we all know". Swedes pay roughly a third of an average salary in income tax, most of it to the municipality and the region, which run schools, healthcare and elder care.

**Själva grundtanken** — *själva* + a definite noun means "the very, the … itself": *själva idén* (the idea itself), *i själva verket* (in actual fact). No extra article is needed in front (Svenska 103, Unit 10).

**Upplever att** (**ÜP-leh-ver aht**) — *uppleva* means "to experience", and in debates "to feel, to perceive". *Många upplever att skolan har blivit sämre* reports a perception, not a fact — a careful, very Swedish way of making a claim (compare the hedging in Unit 4).

**Valdeltagandet** (**VAHL-dehl-tah-gahn-deh**) — turnout in Swedish general elections is usually between 80 and 90 percent. Elections are held every four years in September, and on the same day voters elect the **riksdag** (349 seats), the regional council and the municipal council. A party needs 4 percent of the vote to enter the riksdag.

**Omställningen** (**OM-stel-ning-en**) — "the transition", in political talk almost always short for *den gröna omställningen*, the green transition. **Beroende av** (dependent on) takes *av*, a fixed preposition from Svenska 103, Unit 16.

**Regeringskris vid bordet** — Anna's joke uses the language of politics for a family dinner, a typically Swedish piece of understatement-humor. **Fortsättningen** (the continuation, the rest) is from *fortsätta*: *fortsättning följer* = to be continued.

grammars.title: Describing trends and dependencies
body: Debates about society are full of change and comparison. These patterns let you describe developments precisely.

head: Pattern
Meaning
Example
rows: Det blir **allt varmare**. **Allt fler** väljer tåget.
**Ju fler** som röstar, **desto starkare** blir demokratin.

after: In *ju … desto* sentences the *ju*-part is a subordinate clause, so it keeps straight word order, subject before verb: *Ju längre **man väntar**, desto dyrare blir det.* The *desto*-part has inversion: *desto dyrare **blir det***. In speech *desto* is often replaced by a second *ju*: *ju förr, ju hellre* (the sooner the better).
*Allt* + comparative is far more common in Swedish than "more and more" in English, especially in news language: *allt färre*, *allt dyrare*, *allt vanligare*.

head: Svenska
Pronunciation
English
rows: the principle of public access to official records

blocks.text: Two features of Swedish democracy often surprise newcomers. First, the **offentlighetsprincipen**: since 1766, anyone may ask to read official documents held by a public authority — emails, decisions, even the prime minister's expense reports — unless they are specifically classified. Second, the agencies (*myndigheter*) such as Skatteverket or Försäkringskassan are fairly independent: ministers are not allowed to tell them how to decide individual cases.

After an election, the Speaker of the riksdag (*talmannen*) proposes a prime minister. The candidate does not need a majority in favor, only that a majority does not vote **against** — which is why Sweden often has minority governments relying on support from other parties.

**Flygskam** — the guilt of flying — is a Swedish coinage from 2018 that spread into many languages, the same year Greta Thunberg began her school strike outside the riksdag. The climate debate in Sweden often runs along a city–countryside line: public transport is an easy choice in Stockholm, but not in a village in Norrland. That is exactly the tension Lars and Elin argue about.

blocks.title: Allemansrätten in brief
items: **Du får:** walk, cycle, ski and ride almost anywhere; swim and land a boat; camp a night or two; pick wild berries, mushrooms and flowers that are not protected.
**Du får inte:** enter private gardens (*tomter*); cut down trees or break branches; drive a motor vehicle off-road; disturb animals or leave litter.
**Ta hänsyn** (be considerate) is the key verb: *ta hänsyn till markägaren, till djuren och till andra besökare*.
